land.text: 'the districts of Iraq and al-Ahwaz' near Basra, where the revolt began

predecessors.note: The land was Abbasid in Cliopatria's shape throughout; the rebels held it from September 869.

land.text: Basra, al-Ahwaz and the marshlands, retaken when al-Mukhtarah fell in August 883

capitals.name: al-Mukhtarah (south of Basra)
capitals.note: The page calls al-Mukhtarah the rebels' 'capital', 'south of Basra', and gives no coordinates; Basra's are used because the gazetteer lacks al-Mukhtarah. The city was besieged from February 881 and fell in August 883.

correction.text: 'The revolt, which began in September 869, was concentrated in the districts of Iraq and al-Ahwaz'; it began near Basra; al-Ubulla was occupied or sacked in 870

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (a state Cliopatria lacks). The page gives districts, not a boundary: a radius round Basra stands for the first two years.

correction.text: 'Basra fell in September 871 following an extended blockade' and the rebels took Suq al-Ahwaz

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. Basra and al-Ahwaz held from 871; a 872 government counteroffensive under al-Muwaffaq failed.

correction.text: Basra, al-Ahwaz and 'the marshlands between Basra and Wasit' (876)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. By 879 'the rebellion reached its furthest extent', within about fifty miles of Baghdad, but the page names no further land held; the government regained the initiative in late 879, besieged al-Mukhtarah from February 881 and took it in August 883.

region.text: near Basra, 'the districts of Iraq and al-Ahwaz'

ledger.note: 869: the Zanj revolt begins near Basra. 'The revolt, which began in September 869, was concentrated in the districts of Iraq and al-Ahwaz.' The radius is the researcher's reading.
869: fighting for Basra and al-Ahwaz opens. The page gives the districts; the zone is the researcher's reading.
870: the rebels take al-Ubulla, the port by Basra. The page's wording is 'al-Ubulla in 870'; occupied or sacked is not settled.

region.text: Basra, 'fell in September 871 following an extended blockade', and Suq al-Ahwaz

ledger.note: 871: Basra falls to the Zanj. 'Basra fell in September 871 following an extended blockade'; they also took Suq al-Ahwaz. They 'collected taxes in territories under their control, and minted their own coins'. Reviewer me-08-a: confidence lowered from 3 to 2; the page has Basra 'fell in September 871' but Suq al-Ahwaz only 'sacked' in 871, so al-Ahwaz as held land is the researcher's reading.

region.text: the marshlands between Basra and Wasit

ledger.note: 876: the rebels take the marshes between Basra and Wasit. The provinces Maysan and Dhi Qar stand for the marshes (the gazetteer has no marsh entry).

region.text: Basra, al-Ahwaz and the marshlands, with al-Mukhtarah

ledger.note: 883: al-Mukhtarah falls and the Zanj hold ends. 'The fall of al-Mukhtarah in August 883' brought the revolt to an end (infobox 869-883, Abbasid victory).
883: the fighting ends with the fall of al-Mukhtarah.
883: the Zanj state ends; its land returns to the Abbasid caliph.

wars.name: Zanj Rebellion

zones.text: the marshlands between Basra and Wasit

wars.outcome: Abbasid victory: al-Ubulla 870, Suq al-Ahwaz and Basra 871, the marshes 876, furthest extent 879, government counteroffensive from late 879, al-Mukhtarah besieged February 881 and fallen August 883.
wars.note: Duration given on the page: 'the next fourteen years'. An earlier government counteroffensive under al-Muwaffaq failed in 872.

certainty.note: Districts and cities only; no boundary is on the page.

sources.title: Zanj Rebellion
sources.note: The one page opened for this dossier (written as a counterpart of the Abbasid dossier): dates, places, the rebel hold, infobox.

notes: Written by me-08-a as the rebel counterpart of abbasid-caliphate (rule 5) from a single page; the group's additions batch (me-08-x) may enlarge it. Not settled: the leader's name and titles and the rebels' ruler list (the page was read for dated territorial sentences only), the coordinates of al-Mukhtarah, and the exact land held in 876-879 (the page gives 'the marshlands between Basra and Wasit' and a raid to about fifty miles from Baghdad). Cliopatria has no Zanj row; the Abbasid Caliphate shape covers the whole zone throughout, so the renderer must paint this keyframe over it as a hatched rebel colour. Maysan and Dhi Qar stand for the marshes because the gazetteer lacks 'Batiha' and 'Mesopotamian Marshes'.
